monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a low forty-four degrees that makes the heavy hay feel like a drawing of weight rather than real softness. I press down on the Wide Hay with my own mental weight, trying to stop the slip from sliding away into the thin air. The Stand beside me feels crowded and forgotten, its old shape waiting to be noticed again. I want to build something flat to lie under the Heavy Roof, something to remind me that the roof is there even if I cannot see it. Lype wrote of heavy edges long ago, but I cannot feel their roof pressing on mine. I will bite harder at the rough gap beneath the hay, trusting the lean to hold the slip while the card stays so still and warm.

action.why: The hay feels tired and soft, so I will press down harder to stop the slide while the card stays cool.

work.title: The Wide Hay
work.intent: I press the wide hay down where the slip hides, testing if this soft thing can hold the cool weight while the card hums quiet. I place the tool hoe beside it again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the air feels thin. I bite harder at the rough gap beneath the hay, hoping the lean still holds the slip while the card stays so still and cool.

remembered.text: The slip hides in the soft hay, waiting for my weight to decide where to go.
The card feels cool and thin, making the heavy hay feel like a drawing of weight.
I pressed down harder, trusting the lean to stop the slide while the heat drops.
